sentence: This project studies how genetic variants and small molecules called metabolites can help sort chronic obstructive pulmonary disease into groups.
This project tries to find out what controls how potassium channels cluster together with calcium channels.
This project provides cell sorting and analysis instruments and expertise to cancer researchers using cytometry.
This project builds machine learning methods that analyze complex biomedical data to understand the causes of human diseases.
This project uses tissue imaging and computational methods to study how tumor cells and immune cells are arranged in colorectal cancer.
This project studies why extra copies of chromosome 21 raise the risk of Hirschsprung disease in people with Down Syndrome.
This project studies how a chloride transporter loss in inflammatory bowel disease harms tissue repair and whether a dietary lipid can restore barrier function.
This project uses machine learning and computer models to study how proteins on the cell surface bind to each other.
This project builds an optical nanotweezer and Raman spectroscopy tool to study differences among single tiny particles that cells release.
This project uses human stem cell models to study how changes to histone modifications drive the cell effects of Down syndrome.
This project builds a way to find the molecules that cause leaky lung barriers in acute respiratory distress syndrome.
This project works to bring a vaccine for lymphatic filariasis, a disease caused by helminths, up to the clinical trial stage.
This project studies how colchicine combined with a statin changes coronary plaque in people whose polygenic score shows a high risk of heart attack.
This project studies which molecular mechanisms control the development of meningeal fibroblasts, cells in the layers surrounding the brain.
This project compares how different Oropouche virus isolates infect human placenta tissue and pregnant mice to learn what drives passage from mother to fetus.
This project studies how mutations in one gene cause RNA to end up in the wrong place in stem cell models of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
This project develops a blood test that reads particles released by nervous system cells to tell apart molecular subtypes of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
This project studies how prenatal alcohol and nicotine exposure affects the development of brain microvessels in the fetal brain using optical imaging.
This project studies how childhood lead exposure harms brain function and raises the risk of psychiatric disease, and tests a flavonoid as a treatment.
This project studies how cells lining the lower gastrointestinal tract repurpose themselves to regenerate the intestinal lining after damage.
